title: Decoding the relationship between oxidative stress and antiseizure medications using network pharmacology and molecular docking.
authors: Desai, Malhar; Singh, Sarangthem Dinamani; Nagamani, Selvaraman; Malik, Sunik; Singh, Anju; Kukreti, Ritushree; Kukreti, Shrikant; Grewal, Gurpreet K
one_liner_zh: 该研究用网络药理学和分子对接分析抗癫痫药物与氧化应激相关蛋白的相互作用，但对象为小分子-蛋白而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅分子对接部分方法可借鉴，与课题关联度低。
abstract: Oxidative stress is known to be associated with epilepsy, and antiseizure medication treatment, albeit with limited consensus on the specific oxidative stress pathways/proteins involved. Identifying these can reveal novel therapeutic targets for epilepsy management. This study utilized network pharmacology to identify potential protein targets of carbamazepine and valproic-acid that are implicated in oxidative stress and epilepsy, thereby highlighting their therapeutic potential. Drug targets for carbamazepine and valproic-acid were predicted using SuperPred/SwissTargetPrediction, while genes associated with epilepsy and oxidative stress were obtained from DisGeNET and GeneCards. Common proteins were identified, and a protein-protein interaction network was constructed using STRING, followed by analysis via Cytoscape. Hub proteins identified were EGFR, GSK3B, and STAT3 for carbamazepine, and PTGS2, mTOR, and TLR4 for valproic-acid. Molecular docking revealed a strong binding affinity of carbamazepine to its targets (DeltaG(bind) > - 5 kcal/mol) and binding of valproic-acid to its targets (DeltaG(bind) > - 3 kcal/mol), with PTGS2 showing the strongest interaction with valproic-acid (- 5.06 kcal/mol). These findings underscore EGFR, GSK3B, and STAT3, for carbamazepine and PTGS2, mTOR, and TLR4 for valproic-acid as pivotal therapeutic targets in oxidative stress-associated epilepsy. These identified proteins can be targeted by add on antioxidants to alleviate oxidative stress generated by chronic antiseizure medication.
abstract_zh: 已知氧化应激与癫痫相关，且抗癫痫药物治疗与之相关，但关于所涉及的具体氧化应激通路/蛋白质尚未达成共识。识别这些靶点可为癫痫管理揭示新的治疗靶标。本研究利用网络药理学识别卡马西平（carbamazepine）和丙戊酸（valproic-acid）在氧化应激和癫痫中涉及的潜在蛋白质靶点，从而凸显其治疗潜力。使用SuperPred/SwissTargetPrediction预测卡马西平和丙戊酸的药物靶点，而癫痫和氧化应激相关基因则从DisGeNET和GeneCards获取。识别共同蛋白质，并使用STRING构建蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络，随后通过Cytoscape进行分析。识别出的核心蛋白质为卡马西平的EGFR、GSK3B和STAT3，以及丙戊酸的PTGS2、mTOR和TLR4。分子对接显示卡马西平与其靶点具有强结合亲和力（DeltaG(bind) > - 5 kcal/mol），丙戊酸与其靶点结合（DeltaG(bind) > - 3 kcal/mol），其中PTGS2与丙戊酸相互作用最强（- 5.06 kcal/mol）。这些发现强调卡马西平的EGFR、GSK3B和STAT3，以及丙戊酸的PTGS2、mTOR和TLR4作为氧化应激相关癫痫中的关键治疗靶点。这些识别出的蛋白质可作为添加抗氧化剂的靶点，以减轻慢性抗癫痫药物产生的氧化应激。
